CONCEPTS: Accounts Receivable is money owed for services already billed. AR follow-up works unpaid claims by aging bucket (0–30, 31–60, 61–90, 91–120, 120+) until each is paid, adjusted, or moved to the patient.

Scheduling → eligibility & benefits → authorization → charge capture & coding → claim scrub & submission → rejection work → adjudication → payment posting → denial management/AR follow-up → patient statements → reporting.
Front-end errors (eligibility, auth, demographics) cause roughly half of all denials; fixing them upstream beats working them in AR.
Pull aged AR → prioritize by $ and TFL risk → check payer portal/IVR first, call only if needed → document in standard note → take action (resubmit, appeal, transfer) → set follow-up date.
Sort AR by payer, aging, $ and status. Work high-$ and near-TFL first. Group by denial type to fix root causes in bulk.
Claim with no errors, adjudicable without extra info. Target first-pass clean claim rate ≥ 95%.
Rejection: failed front-end edits, never adjudicated → fix and send as NEW claim (no appeal). Denial: adjudicated with $0 → corrected claim or appeal.
Rejections do NOT stop the timely filing clock.
Corrected claim: our data was wrong (code, modifier, Dx, NPI). Freq code 7 replace, 8 void, with original ICN in box 22 / REF F8. Appeal: data was right, payer decision is wrong.
Medicare does not accept freq 7 for Part B—use reopening (phone/portal) or redetermination.
Total AR ÷ (charges in period ÷ days in period). Benchmark < 40 days; > 50 is a problem.
Days in AR; % AR > 90 days (target < 15–20%); clean claim rate; denial rate (target < 5–10%); first-pass resolution; net collection rate (target ≥ 95%); cost to collect.
Medicare Parts A, B, C, D
A: inpatient, SNF, hospice, home health. B: physician, outpatient, DME, labs. C: Medicare Advantage (private plans replace A/B). D: prescription drugs.
Part B premium $202.90/mo; Part B deductible $283; Part A inpatient deductible $1,736. After Part B deductible, patient owes 20% coinsurance.

MEDICARE: How Medicare processes Part B claims

Claim → MAC front-end edits (999/277CA rejections) → CWF eligibility/MSP/hospice checks → NCCI/MUE/LCD edits → adjudication → ERA/MSN. Know your MAC (Noridian, Novitas, Palmetto, NGS, WPS, CGS, First Coast) — each has its own portal, IVR and LCDs.
Unprocessable claims (CO-16 + MA130)
No appeal rights. Read the second RARC (e.g. N290, M51, MA120). Fix the element and send as a brand-new claim. Don't use a reopening or redetermination.
Reopenings vs redeterminations

Reopening: minor clerical errors (wrong DOS, modifier, units, Dx) within 1 year of initial determination. Done by phone/IVR/portal; fastest route. Redetermination: disagreement with decision, 120 days from receipt of initial determination, MAC level-1 appeal (CMS-20027 or portal).
Appeal ladder

1) Redetermination – MAC, 120 days. 2) Reconsideration – QIC, 180 days. 3) ALJ hearing – 60 days, minimum amount in controversy (adjusted yearly). 4) Medicare Appeals Council – 60 days. 5) Federal district court – 60 days, higher amount threshold.
Medicare Advantage is different

MA plans follow their own appeal path: provider payment dispute or reconsideration with the plan (usually 60–65 days for non-contracted). From 2026 (CMS-0057-F), MA plans must decide standard prior auth in 7 days, expedited in 72 hours, and give a specific denial reason.
MSP / CWF rejections

Claim denies when CWF shows another primary (EGHP, auto, WC). Action: confirm with patient, have them call BCRC (1-855-798-2627) to update MSP record, or bill the primary. Provider can't update MSP records directly except via MSP questionnaire at intake.
Hospice overlap

Patient elected hospice → services related to terminal illness pay through hospice. Attending physician not employed by hospice: GV. Unrelated condition: GW. Check election date on eligibility (HETS).
Home health / SNF consolidated billing
During a home health episode or Part A SNF stay, many services must be billed by the HHA/SNF (consolidated billing). Outside providers bill the facility, not Medicare.
3-day payment window

Outpatient diagnostic and related non-diagnostic services within 3 days before an inpatient admission at the same hospital are bundled into the inpatient claim (1 day for non-IPPS hospitals). Physician services: PD modifier.
ABN workflow

Give ABN (CMS-R-131) before service when you expect denial for necessity/frequency. GA = ABN given; GZ = expected denial, no ABN (provider liable); GY = statutorily excluded (no ABN needed); GX = voluntary ABN for excluded service.
LCD/NCD medical necessity
Look up the LCD on the Medicare Coverage Database and its billing & coding article—covered ICD-10 list lives there. N115/N386 RARCs point to them.
PECOS ordering/referring
Labs, imaging, DME, home health need ordering/referring provider in PECOS with eligible specialty. Denial: CO-183 + N264/N265.
Timely filing
12 months from DOS. Exceptions: administrative error by Medicare, retroactive Medicare entitlement, retro Medicaid disenrollment to MA. Request exception with documentation.
Medicare audits
TPE (targeted probe & educate), RAC (post-payment, complex review), UPIC (fraud), CERT (error-rate sampling). ADR letters: respond within 45 days or claim denies (CO-50/N102).
WISeR model (2026–2031)

Prior authorization for selected Original Medicare services in WA, NJ, OH, OK, TX, AZ, run by contractors using AI-assisted review. Services without the required review face pre-payment medical review. Check the CMS WISeR page for the current service list.
Sequestration & payment math
Medicare pays 80% of allowed after deductible, minus 2% sequestration on the payment. Example: allowed $100, deductible met → $80 × 0.98 = $78.40 paid; patient 20% = $20.
QMB protection
Providers can't bill QMB patients for Medicare deductible/coinsurance; bill Medicaid or write off. Eligibility response shows QMB status via HETS.
Medicare common rejection reasons
Invalid MBI/name mismatch, patient not eligible on DOS, MSP primary, hospice/HH overlap, provider not enrolled/PTAN mismatch, NPI/PTAN pairing, ordering not in PECOS, invalid ICD-10, missing CLIA.
UHC: UHC Smart Edits — what they are
Pre-adjudication checks on claims sent through EDI or the UHC Provider Portal. They flag likely errors and documentation needs within about 24 hours, so you can fix the claim before it denies.
Smart Edit response codes (277CA)

Return Edit A3:21: claim returned; fix and resubmit. Rejection Edit A7:21: claim rejected. Duplicate rejection A3:54. COB rejection A7:85. Informational Edit A1:19: no action needed, but review it. Messages start with P4999 followed by a mnemonic that names the edit, e.g. P4999mPI (physician interpretation code billed in the wrong POS).
How to work Smart Edits

Check the 277CA report daily. Read the mnemonic and resolution text. Correct the claim and resubmit as a new claim, not a corrected claim, because returned claims were never adjudicated. If the claim is correct, follow the edit's instructions; some edits time out and adjudicate as billed if no action is taken. Documentation Edits arrive by email, TrackIt and EDI; upload records through the portal.
Common Smart Edit themes
CLIA mismatches, exact duplicates, COB other-coverage, POS vs professional/technical component, modifier 25/59 usage, NCCI pairs, missing NDC, diagnosis-to-procedure, frequency.
UHC payer IDs

Commercial & MA: 87726. Many UHC Community Plan (Medicaid) states use 87726 too, but some have separate IDs. UMR: 39026. Surest: 25463. Optum/affiliates differ. Always check the ID card's back and UHC's payer list.
UHC reimbursement policies that drive denials

ED facility E/M level policy (algorithmic level assignment), modifier 25 review, consultation codes not paid (bill E/M instead, Medicare-like), CMS-based NCCI/MUE edits, assistant surgeon, telehealth policy, same-day E/M, NDC requirement, prolonged services. Policies are published monthly in the Network Bulletin; MA reimbursement policies are in UHC's monthly RPUB.
UHC prior authorization

Via UHC Provider Portal (Prior Authorization & Notification). Gold Card program exempts qualifying groups for selected codes. Radiology/cardiology/oncology may route to Optum or other vendors. UHC said it would reduce PA on about 30% of applicable services under the 2025 industry pledge; AMA survey data suggests limited practical relief.
UHC reconsideration vs appeal

Step 1, claim reconsideration: for corrected info or a disagreement, submitted through the portal claim (Claims → Reconsideration), with attachments. Step 2, appeal: if reconsideration is upheld. Time limits are in the UHC Administrative Guide and vary by product (commercial, MA, Community Plan); confirm on the call.
UMR (UHC TPA)

Self-funded employer plans administered by UMR. Different phone numbers and rules from UHC; the IVR asks for a passcode generated from the UMR portal before you reach a rep. Plan rules vary by employer group.
UHC Community Plan (Medicaid)
State-specific: follow state Medicaid rules (no patient billing, state TFL). Some states route behavioral health to Optum.
Recurring UHC denial patterns

CO-4/CO-11 smart-edit misses, CO-197 auth, CO-50 E/M level and ED level reviews, CO-252 records requests (documentation edits), CO-22 COB questionnaires (member must answer every 12 months), CO-109 for MA members billed to Medicare.
